description:
Approved scope: PRD Phase 1 Connect foundation plus backend functions needed by later Person self-service. Planning only in this pass. Include schema migrations for Connect (NOT AI credential migration), generic resolver, authenticated Person grant operations, OAuth start/callback/reconnect/refresh, safe mutation events, Person merge/deletion, security and tests. Exclude AIProviderCredential association/backfill, Factory/ProviderSpec/ServerManager changes, actual Agent invalidation, BO screens, Person screens/session implementation, Data Source/MCP adoption, and workflow Actor propagation. These remain separate slices.

Infrastructure audit: actual namespace is Zaq.Engine.Connect. credential.ex owns reusable provider configuration; grant.ex owns context-bound grants. Existing grants require resource_type/resource_id, owners org/user, auth kinds api_key/oauth2/jwt_bearer, and have no ownership uniqueness. Existing Credential also stores API-key/JWT secrets. OAuth and refresh already exist; Engine API exposes internal Connect operations. ActorNormalizer normalizes rather than authenticates. People.delete_person and PersonMerger currently omit Connect grants. Existing routing is not a durable transactional outbox; Oban is available.

Architecture decisions: add a credential-bound grant lane without rewriting legacy resource-bound consumers; no provider-wide matching; no new resolver fallback to secrets on Credential. Keep user ownership and user_level unchanged. One current credential-bound grant row per credential and owner across all statuses; revoke retains the row and blocks optional fallback, explicit removal permits absence/fallback. Historical events retain IDs, not secrets. Person FK is a dedicated person_id constrained equal to owner_id for person ownership; never apply a people FK to polymorphic user IDs. Use partial unique indexes for person and org canonical rows, handling NULL org owner IDs explicitly. Changes remain opt-in; existing resource-bound selection and AI runtime are untouched.

Security: trusted execution actor may reach internal resolver; Person management must require authenticated Person context from a trusted adapter, never an arbitrary request map. Nil actor selects global only in privileged runtime resolution; nil never authorizes management or reveals secrets. Public/event management replies use allowlisted DTOs. ResolvedCredential is internal runtime-only, redacted, and never emitted via generic read actions. Credential-owned OAuth client settings never become Person-editable. API key/private key/token inputs are write-only and strictly encrypted. No raw provider error bodies, authorization codes, token payloads, or unrestricted metadata in responses/events/telemetry.

Compatibility: preserve current consumers while introducing explicit canonical management APIs. Policy/global-grant completeness validation applies at the new atomic configuration boundary, not retrospectively to every legacy credential changeset. JWT credential-required secret validation must support canonical grant-owned JWT material without weakening existing legacy mode. No migration copies company credentials to People. Later AI migration must populate canonical grants before switching reads.

Delivery: test-first issues, one focused PR per issue where practical, no implementation until planning dependencies are validated. OAuth and refresh are split because of independent security/concurrency surfaces; identity cleanup is a separate Accounts-owned integration. Keep a serial dependency chain to provide safe delivery gates; it is intentionally stricter than theoretical parallelism, without diamonds. Documentation and tests accompany every step. Require >=95% touched-file coverage or explicit measured exception and follow-up, mix format after code edits, focused tests and final mix q.

Follow-on contracts: mutation delivery provides secret-free credential/person/grant dependencies and monotonic revision/event identity for later distributed Agent consumers. This slice does not claim to invalidate Agents or provide end-to-end BYOK. Future Agent subscriber must ensure all owning nodes receive events and close server-creation-versus-invalidation races; single NodeRouter invocation is not evidence of broadcast. Workflow scope actor work is not a prerequisite to testing Connect directly. Coordinate identity compatibility with zaq-r35/zaq-u3g and coverage debt zaq-c1k.

Open delivery gate: before enabling public self-service endpoints, identify and verify the trusted Person session adapter; if none exists, ship tested backend functions only and document that transport adapter as deferred. Do not invent a Person login system in this slice. Architecture approval is the user Go following the seven-step foundation outline; implementation refinements that materially change product/security semantics require renewed approval.

comments.text: Plan expanded into nine independently reviewable steps: approved step 2 split into canonical mutations and durable events; approved step 5 split into OAuth authorization and refresh. Serial delivery is intentional to avoid exposing unsafe partial personal flows. Mermaid sequence: graph LR; S1[Storage] --> S2[Mutations]; S2 --> S3[Events]; S3 --> S4[Resolver]; S4 --> S5[Person API]; S5 --> S6[OAuth]; S6 --> S7[Refresh]; S7 --> S8[Person lifecycle]; S8 --> S9[Validation]. Planning only: application files unchanged; implementation tasks remain open. Existing Beadwork searches for person grant, credential policy and Connect foundation found no matching active plan.

Dependency validation completed: exact blocked_by/blocks edges verified for all nine issues, all five required planning sections present, serial DAG acyclic with no diamonds. Open epics hide children in bw ready; epic activated for plan tracking, then bw ready confirmed zaq-jrg.1 as sole ready child. All implementation children remain open and no application changes have started.

Planning closeout: mix q completed with exit 0 (docs generation and Credo: 1177 source files, no issues). git status --short clean afterward. No application code changed, no commits or PR created. This check is baseline validation, not evidence that planned feature tests exist or pass.
